newsitem.title: DENMARK: U.S. data send Danish bond prices up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. data send Danish bond prices up.

text.p: Lower-than-expected U.S inflation data sent Danish bond prices upward on Friday and dealers expected the trend to continue on Monday.
"The market reacted favourably to the American data and Europe in general looks good," a senior dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 closed at 105.50, up 0.58 point from Thursday's close.
Its September future rose 0.48 point to 105.48, with 133 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.20 point t0 83.05.
The crown traded at 3.8525 to the mark, firming slightly from its opening 3.8532.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed to 95 basis points from 97 this morning. --Claus Mathisen, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969652
